cases.question: How sure is the forecast for 48 hours from now?
cases.answer: For the 25-48 hour live track record bucket, the forecast has a mean absolute error (MAE) of 8.8 and a skill score of 45.4% versus CAMS. In backtesting at the exact 48-hour lead time, the MAE is 6.402 with an 80% range coverage of 81.2%.

cases.question: How accurate has this forecast actually been?
cases.answer: Our published live forecasts (scored against OpenAQ ground measurements) have achieved an overall MAE of 8.556 µg/m³, beating CAMS on 73 of 76 days with an overall skill score of 46.3% over CAMS and 39.1% over persistence. The 80% uncertainty range achieved 75.1% coverage with a mean width of 28.64. In our rolling-origin backtests, mean skill reached 45.9% over CAMS with range coverage between 81.1% and 83.1% across lead times.

cases.question: Is this better than the Copernicus CAMS forecast?
cases.answer: Yes, the live track record shows this system beats the Copernicus CAMS forecast with an overall skill score of 0.463 (beating CAMS in 73 of 76 days). Across all scored points, our MAE is 8.556 compared to CAMS MAE of 15.945.

cases.question: What is the backtested error at 72 hours?
cases.answer: At the 72-hour lead time, the backtested MAE is 6.789, with an R² of 0.579 and an 80% range coverage of 82.6%. In live tracking for the 49–72 hour bucket, the MAE is 9.749 with a bias of -2.264 and an interval coverage of 75.1%.

cases.question: How good is the 1-hour forecast?
cases.answer: For the 1-6 hour live track record bucket, the forecast has an MAE of 6.1 and a skill score of 65.5% versus CAMS. In the rolling-origin backtest, the 1-hour lead time has an MAE of 2.7, an R² of 0.93, and 82.7% coverage of the 80% range.

cases.question: What drives the forecast the most?
cases.answer: The 24-hour forecast is driven most by measured minus CAMS (now) with a mean SHAP value of 6.13, followed by CAMS forecast for target hour at 4.11, and forecast wind speed at 3.12. Other top factors include measured PM2.5 3h mean (2.8), CAMS PM10 (1.63), wind dispersion (1.39), forecast temperature (1.28), and CAMS PM2.5 (now) at 1.21.

cases.question: Why does the model use CAMS as an input if CAMS is wrong?
cases.answer: Even though CAMS can be imperfect, our model uses it as a valuable baseline signal, beating CAMS in 73 of 76 days with an overall skill vs CAMS of 0.463 and an overall MAE of 8.556 compared to CAMS's 15.945. In backtesting, the model achieves a mean skill vs CAMS of 0.459, successfully correcting and improving upon raw CAMS outputs.
